target.title: fix(agents): route llama.cpp GBNF cleaning through provider tool-schema hooks
target.body:
Fixes #108367
Fixes #108473
Fixes #108580

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw runs against a llama.cpp-backed endpoint with grammar-constrained tool calling, chat requests fail with HTTP 400 before inference whenever the active tool list includes GBNF-hostile JSON Schema constructs (#108580):

1. Unanchored / PCRE-shorthand `pattern` (e.g. `\\S`)
2. `maxLength` above llama.cpp's ~2000 GBNF repetition ceiling (e.g. cron `trigger.script` `65536`)

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical tool schemas keep their server-side validation guidance. Cleaning happens only on llama.cpp-compatible routes:

| Activation path | Who owns it |
|---|---|
| Bundled `ollama`, `ollama-cloud`, `lmstudio`, `llama-cpp` | Provider-owned `normalizeToolSchemas` via `buildProviderToolCompatFamilyHooks("llamacpp-gbnf")` |
| Custom OpenAI-compatible llama.cpp endpoints | Opt-in `modelCompat.toolSchemaProfile: "llamacpp"` |
| Ordinary providers (`openai`, etc.) | Unchanged — canonical `pattern` / `maxLength` retained |

Shared-core provider-ID guessing was removed (ClawSweeper P1). This mirrors the Gemini family-helper pattern in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-tools`.

## User Impact

llama.cpp / Ollama / LM Studio users can keep cron and related tools enabled without pre-inference grammar 400s. OpenAI and other providers keep model-facing length/pattern constraints.

## Evidence

### Exact-head bundled-provider live proof (head `9ac84e3e042`)

This run registered the real bundled Ollama plugin, selected its provider-owned `normalizeToolSchemas` hook, printed the outbound schema, and sent that schema to a local `llama-server` b9960. Private endpoint details are omitted.

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/exact-head-gbnf-live-proof.test.ts --reporter=verbose
EXACT_HEAD=9ac84e3e042
PROVIDER_HOOK=ollama
OUTBOUND_SCHEMA={"type":"object","properties":{"declarationKey":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":200},"script":{"type":"string","minLength":1}}}
LLAMA_SERVER_HTTP=200
INFERENCE_RESPONSE={"choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"ready"}}],...}

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
```

This proves the current bundled-provider activation path: `pattern` and oversized `maxLength: 65536` are absent from the outbound schema, `maxLength: 200` remains, and llama-server successfully reaches inference.

### Focused tests
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  packages/ai/src/providers/clean-for-llamacpp-gbnf.test.ts \
  packages/ai/src/providers/agent-tools-parameter-schema.llamacpp.test.ts \
  src/plugin-sdk/provider-tools.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/tool-schema-llamacpp-compat.test.ts \
  extensions/ollama/index.test.ts \
  extensions/lmstudio/index.test.ts \
  extensions/llama-cpp/index.test.ts
```
All green on Node 22.

### Live llama-server regression transcript (shipped failure)
Earlier local `llama-server` b9960 run against the shipped grammar-hostile cron schema:

- unanchored `\\S` → HTTP 400 `Pattern must start with '^' and end with '$'`
- `maxLength: 65536` → HTTP 400 `failed to parse grammar`
- cleaned schema (same projection the provider hook now emits) → HTTP 200, inference proceeds

The cleaned payload that reached HTTP 200 is exactly what `normalizeLlamacppGbnfToolSchemas` / `toolSchemaProfile: "llamacpp"` emit on this head.

### vs #108671
#108671 removes constraints from canonical tool schemas globally. This PR preserves them and cleans only on llama.cpp-compatible provider/profile routes — the ownership ClawSweeper recommended.
